Text: Java integer division happens when {{c1::both operands are integer types}}.
Extra: The receiving variable type does not change the expression result after the expression has already been evaluated.

Text: `7 / 3` with `int` operands evaluates to {{c1::2}}.
Extra: The fractional part is discarded.

Text: `17 % 5` evaluates to {{c1::2}}.
If either operand of `+` is a `String`, Java performs {{c1::string concatenation}}.
Extra: The other operand is converted to text.

Text: `=` means {{c1::assignment}}, while `==` means {{c2::comparison}}.
Extra: Mixing these is a common beginner bug.

Text: Comparison operators produce a {{c1::boolean}} result.
Extra: They do not produce `0` or `1` in Java.

Text: For object references, `==` checks {{c1::reference equality}}.
Extra: It asks whether both references point to the same object.

Text: For `String` content equality, usually use {{c1::.equals()}}.
Extra: `==` is not content comparison for objects.

Text: `&&` short-circuits when the left-hand side is {{c1::false}}.
Extra: False AND anything is false.

Text: `||` short-circuits when the left-hand side is {{c1::true}}.
Extra: True OR anything is true.

Text: Boolean `&` and `|` evaluate {{c1::both sides}}.
Extra: They do not short-circuit.

Text: Postfix `i++` uses the {{c1::old value}} first, then increments.
Extra: This matters only when the expression value is used.

Text: Prefix `++i` increments first, then uses the {{c1::new value}}.
Extra: This differs from postfix in larger expressions.

Text: A {{c1::side effect}} is a change that happens while evaluating code.
Extra: Examples include incrementing a variable or mutating an object.

Text: The ternary operator structure is {{c1::condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse}}.
Extra: It chooses one of two expressions.

Text: `instanceof` returns {{c1::false}} when the left-hand expression is `null`.
Extra: Null is not an instance of any class.

Text: Pattern matching for `instanceof` checks the type and declares a {{c1::typed variable}}.
Extra: Example: `value instanceof String text`.

Text: Operator {{c1::precedence}} decides which operators group first.
Extra: Parentheses can override it.

Text: Operator {{c1::associativity}} decides grouping when operators have the same precedence.
Extra: Most arithmetic operators associate left-to-right.

Text: Assignment operators associate {{c1::right-to-left}}.
Extra: This is why `a = b = 10` works.

Text: `2 + 3 * 4` evaluates to {{c1::14}}.
Extra: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition.
Parentheses override precedence.
